title: Transition Topology, Network Flow & Persistence — Rigorous Analogues for Door/Loop/Threshold Research
status: mathematical analogue layer; not physical validation
purpose: Identify mathematical tools that genuinely clarify the project's transition, loop, evidence and network problems: max-flow/min-cut for bottlenecks, bifurcation for qualitative regime change, Morse theory for topology change at critical values, and persistent homology for features that survive across evidence/scale filtrations.
epistemic_boundary: These are standard mathematical frameworks that can be applied to project data. Their applicability does not prove Potatoverse cosmology, divine identity, biblical prediction, neuroanatomical symbolism or a new physical law. A physical claim requires independently defined measurable variables and empirical tests.

modules.standard_math: In a capacitated network, maximum source-to-sink flow equals the capacity of a minimum cut separating source and sink.
modules.project_use: Model access/capability bottlenecks. A narrow Gate can be represented as low-capacity connection; adding redundant paths can improve resilience; a protective boundary can deliberately restrict hostile flow while preserving desired flow.
modules.formal_sketch: G=(V,E,c); maxflow(s,t)=mincut(s,t). Changing a Door/edge capacity c_e changes reachable throughput without changing metaphysical meaning.
useful_questions: Does one Door create a single point of failure?
Would adding another route increase resilience?
Which boundary edges must be crossed to connect two clusters?

modules.standard_math: A parameter-dependent dynamical system can change qualitative behavior when a control parameter crosses a bifurcation value.
modules.project_use: Distinguish gradual displacement from genuine regime change. A threshold event should be called a bifurcation only when a defined model's qualitative solution/attractor/stability structure changes as a parameter varies.
modules.formal_sketch: dx/dt=F(x,lambda); lambda=lambda_c can separate qualitatively non-equivalent regimes.
modules.project_distinction: Door/threshold language can be compared with bifurcation only after the state variable, parameter and qualitative regimes are specified.

modules.standard_math: Morse theory studies topology through critical points/critical values of a scalar function on a manifold; topology of level/sublevel structures changes at critical values under standard hypotheses.
modules.project_use: A stronger mathematical analogue for a topology-changing Door than a generic circle metaphor: as a threshold parameter crosses a critical value, previously separated regions/components/handles can change connectivity/topology.
modules.formal_sketch: M_a={x | f(x)<=a}; compare topology of M_a as a crosses critical values of f.
modules.project_distinction: The critical value is mathematically meaningful only after f and the state space are defined; symbolic thresholds do not become Morse critical points by analogy alone.

modules.standard_math: Persistent homology tracks topological features as a filtered complex changes, recording feature birth/death intervals across filtration values.
modules.project_use: Analyze whether archive structure survives changes in evidence threshold or scale. Build the graph/complex first from high-confidence provenance, then progressively include weaker/inferred relations and observe which connected components, loops or higher-order features persist.
modules.formal_sketch: K_0 subseteq K_1 subseteq ... subseteq K_n; feature persistence interval [birth,death) records how long a homological feature survives the filtration.
candidate_filtrations: chronological reveal: only evidence known by date t
modules.interpretation: A feature that persists under stricter/multiple filtrations is structurally robust in the dataset. That means robust-to-encoding/evidence-threshold, not historically true or supernatural.

new_archive_tests.procedure: Build overlap graph using only P=5 rows, then P>=4, P>=3, etc.; record components/bridges/loops that appear or disappear.
new_archive_tests.meaning: Separates structures already visible in strongest evidence from those dependent on conversation recovery/later synthesis.

new_archive_tests.procedure: Rebuild graph cumulatively by project date and separately by discovery date.
new_archive_tests.meaning: Shows when structures became available to the project versus when the archive recognized them; prevents hindsight collapse.

new_archive_tests.procedure: Remove top-betweenness or articulation nodes and measure component fragmentation; then compare with low-degree countertexts.
new_archive_tests.meaning: Distinguishes popular motifs from actual structural bridges and from ethically indispensable constraints.

new_archive_tests.procedure: Assign provisional non-theological capacities to data/institution edges only where empirical throughput/availability exists; recompute min cuts under edge removal.
new_archive_tests.meaning: Useful for North/economic/infrastructure graphs; do not assign mystical capacities to biblical symbols.

cross_project_epiphanies: A Door can be formalized in several inequivalent ways: edge toggle, edge creation, cut removal, capacity change, or critical-value topology change. The model should state which one it means.
A loop's existence is less informative than its persistence across scale/evidence thresholds. This gives the project a rigorous way to distinguish fragile pattern-matching from structural recurrence.
The evidence hierarchy itself can become a filtration: strong-source structure first, weaker-source structure later. This makes archive epistemics computational rather than rhetorical.
Redundancy can be beneficial: a system with multiple routes may be more resilient than a single sacred bottleneck. High betweenness is therefore both bridge power and failure risk.
A threshold is not automatically a phase transition. Bifurcation/criticality language should be reserved for defined models with demonstrable qualitative change.
